\chapter{Nerves before a big day}
\label{ch:ar-nerves-before-a-big-day}
\hlchaptermodality{497}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that someone is tense, unsettled or hesitant, and that someone got flustered or held back a feeling.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 497: I can say that someone is tense, unsettled or hesitant, and that someone got flustered or held back a feeling.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{متوتر} (mutawattir)}{متوتر (mutawattir)}]{\ar{متوتر} (mutawattir) — tense, nervous}

\label{lesson:AR-C497-mutawattir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for at ease, then the Arabic for to feel relieved.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{متوتر}}
\textbf{\ar{متوتر}} — \emph{mutawattir} — \textquotedblleft{}tense, nervous\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{أختي} \ar{متوترة} \ar{قبل} \ar{المقابلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat ukhtī mutawattira qabla al-muqābala.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister was nervous before the interview.
\end{quote}

The noun \ar{توتر}, stress, shares the root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{متوتر}} (\emph{mutawattir}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-t-r}, \textquotedblleft{}a bowstring\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mutawattir is the participle of Form V: drawn tight, like a bowstring.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mutawattir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mutawattir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat ukhtī mutawattira qabla al-muqābala.} — My sister was nervous before the interview.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for at ease, then the Arabic for to feel relieved, then say \emph{mutawattir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{متوتر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Tense, nervous\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ارتبك} (irtabaka)}{ارتبك (irtabaka)}]{\ar{ارتبك} (irtabaka) — to get flustered}

\label{lesson:AR-C497-irtabaka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to feel relieved, then the Arabic for tense.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ارتبك}}
\textbf{\ar{ارتبك}} — \emph{irtabaka} — \textquotedblleft{}to get flustered\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ارتبك} \ar{الطالب} \ar{ونسي} \ar{الجواب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{irtabaka aṭ-ṭālib wa-nasiya al-jawāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The student got flustered and forgot the answer.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرتبك}, \emph{yartabik}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ارتبك}} (\emph{irtabaka}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-b-k}, \textquotedblleft{}to be mixed up, entangled\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form VIII irtabaka is to become tangled: to lose one's thread.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtabaka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtabaka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtabaka aṭ-ṭālib wa-nasiya al-jawāb.} — The student got flustered and forgot the answer.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to feel relieved, then the Arabic for tense, then say \emph{irtabaka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ارتبك} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get flustered\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مضطرب} (muḍṭarib)}{مضطرب (muḍṭarib)}]{\ar{مضطرب} (muḍṭarib) — agitated, unsettled}

\label{lesson:AR-C497-mudtarib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for tense, then the Arabic for to get flustered.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مضطرب}}
\textbf{\ar{مضطرب}} — \emph{muḍṭarib} — \textquotedblleft{}agitated, unsettled\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{البحر} \ar{مضطربا} \ar{في} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-baḥr muḍṭariban fī al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sea was rough in the night.
\end{quote}

It is said of a person, the sea or the weather.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مضطرب}} (\emph{muḍṭarib}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-r-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to strike, to beat\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Muḍṭarib is the participle of Form VIII, where the t turns into ṭ: one beaten about, restless.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḍṭarib}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḍṭarib}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-baḥr muḍṭariban fī al-layl.} — The sea was rough in the night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for tense, then the Arabic for to get flustered, then say \emph{muḍṭarib} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مضطرب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Agitated, unsettled\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{متردد} (mutaraddid)}{متردد (mutaraddid)}]{\ar{متردد} (mutaraddid) — hesitant}

\label{lesson:AR-C497-mutaraddid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to get flustered, then the Arabic for agitated.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{متردد}}
\textbf{\ar{متردد}} — \emph{mutaraddid} — \textquotedblleft{}hesitant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الزبون} \ar{مترددا} \ar{بين} \ar{القميصين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna az-zabūn mutaraddidan bayna al-qamīṣayn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The customer was hesitating between the two shirts.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{متردد}} (\emph{mutaraddid}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to send back, to return\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mutaraddid is the participle of Form V: one who goes back and forth.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mutaraddid}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna az-zabūn mutaraddidan bayna al-qamīṣayn.} — The customer was hesitating between the two shirts.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to get flustered, then the Arabic for agitated, then say \emph{mutaraddid} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كتم} (katama)}{كتم (katama)}]{\ar{كتم} (katama) — to hold back (a feeling)}

\label{lesson:AR-C497-katama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for agitated, then the Arabic for hesitant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كتم}}
\textbf{\ar{كتم}} — \emph{katama} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold back (a feeling)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كتمت} \ar{البنت} \ar{ضحكتها} \ar{في} \ar{الصف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{katamat al-bint ḍaḥkatahā fī aṣ-ṣaff.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The girl held back her laugh in class.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يكتم}, \emph{yaktum}.

It also means to keep a secret: \ar{كتم} \ar{السر}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كتم}} (\emph{katama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-t-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to conceal, to keep secret\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives yaktumu as its present.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{katama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{katamat al-bint ḍaḥkatahā fī aṣ-ṣaff.} — The girl held back her laugh in class.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for agitated, then the Arabic for hesitant, then say \emph{katama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
